**2. DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS**

2.1 **Ticket**: A formal record in FAMS tracking a discrete unit of field work from request through completion, including status changes and internal comments.

2.2 **Status**: The current lifecycle stage of a ticket as defined in Section 4.2.

2.3 **APU**: Anti-Poaching Unit.

2.4 **TCRZ**: Tiger Corridor Restoration Zone.

2.5 **FAMS**: Field Activity Management System (electronic platform used by NESCP).

2.6 **Field Officer (FO)**: Any NESCP staff member authorised to create or update tickets.

2.7 **Range Officer (RO)**: The officer in charge of a designated forest range or operational area.

2.8 **Director**: The NESCP Director, who holds final revision authority for this Manual.

---

**3. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

3.1 **NESCP Director**
- Holds the authority to approve revisions to this Manual.
- Resolves disputes regarding ticket priority, escalation, or closure.
- Reviews quarterly summary reports on ticket completion rates.

3.2 **Range Officer (RO)**
- Approves ticket requests within their range.
- Assigns Field Officers to tasks.
- Verifies the accuracy of closure reports before final approval.

3.4 **FAMS Administrator**
- Maintains user accounts and access permissions.
- Ensures system backups are taken daily at 18:00 IST.
- Flags tickets with no status change for 14 days to the relevant RO.

3.5 **Partner Organisations**
- Must follow the ticket lifecycle and reporting standards in this Manual when operating within NESCP areas.
- May be granted limited access to FAMS as per agreements with the Director.

---

**4. TICKET LIFECYCLE**

4.2 **Status Definitions**

| Status | Code | Definition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Draft | D | Ticket created but not yet submitted for approval. |
| Submitted | S | Ticket sent to RO for review. |
| Approved | A | RO has approved the ticket; work may commence. |
| In Progress | IP | Work has started; field team is active. |
| On Hold | OH | Work paused due to weather, wildlife conflict, or resource shortage. Reason must be noted in comments. |
| Awaiting Closure | AC | Work complete; closure report pending verification. |
| Closed | C | Closure report verified and accepted by RO. |
| Rejected | R | Ticket not approved; reason noted in comments. |

4.3 **Status Change Rules**
- Only the ticket creator or the relevant RO may change status.
- Every status change must be accompanied by a dated internal comment (see Section 4.5).
- A ticket may remain in Draft or On Hold for no more than 30 days without a mandatory review comment.

4.4 **Internal Comments**
- Internal comments are append-only and cannot be edited or deleted.
- Comments must include the author's name, role, and date in the following format: `[Name/Role/DD-MM-YYYY] Comment text`.
- Comments are visible to all NESCP staff with FAMS access but are not part of the official closure report.

4.5 **Closure**
- Upon completion of field work, the FO must attach the closure report (including photographic evidence where applicable) and set status to Awaiting Closure.
- The RO must verify the report within 7 working days, after which the status is set to Closed.
- If the report is found deficient, the RO sets the status to On Hold with a comment specifying the deficiency.

---

**5. OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES**

5.1 **Patrol Operations**
- All patrols must have a ticket in Approved status before departure.
- Patrol logs (route, sightings, incidents) must be uploaded to the ticket within 24 hours of return.
6.1 **Equipment Issuance**
- Equipment is issued by the Store Keeper upon presentation of an approved ticket.
- Any equipment not returned within 7 days of ticket closure will be reported to the RO.
- Damaged equipment must be returned with a written note describing the cause of damage.

6.2 **Safety Protocols**
- No staff member may enter the field alone after dark unless accompanied by a second staff member and with prior RO approval.
- First-aid kits must be carried on all patrols and deployments.
- In case of snakebite, the nearest medical facility must be contacted immediately, and the RO notified within 1 hour.
- All staff must complete a basic wilderness first-aid refresher course annually.

---

**7. REPORTING AND RECORDS**

7.1 **Field Reports**
- Field reports must be submitted in English or the local language, as per the ticket instructions.
- Reports must include the ticket number, date, location (with GPS coordinates), and a summary of activities.
- Photographic evidence must be embedded in the report where applicable.

7.2 **Equipment Logs**
- Equipment logs must be updated at each issue and return, noting the condition of the equipment.
- Battery levels for GPS units and cameras must be recorded at the start of each field day.

7.3 **Incident Reports**
- Any incident involving injury, wildlife conflict, or damage to property must be reported in writing within 24 hours.
- Incident reports must include a timeline of events and a list of witnesses, if any.

---

**8. TRAINING AND CAPACITY BUILDING**

8.1 **Mandatory Trainings**
- All field staff must complete the following trainings within 6 months of joining:
  - Basic GPS and map reading
  - Cam trap setup and maintenance
  - Wildlife conflict mitigation
  - Data entry and FAMS usage

8.2 **Refresher Courses**
- Refresher courses are held twice a year, in April and October.
- Attendance is recorded in the staff member's training log, which is reviewed during annual performance appraisals.

8.3 **New Staff Induction**
- New staff must be accompanied by a senior FO for their first three patrols.
- Induction checklists must be signed by both the new staff member and the supervising officer.

**5. CAM TRAP MONITORING**

5.1 Cam traps are deployed for wildlife monitoring, population estimation, and detecting the presence of tigers and other key species.

5.2 As per revision 1.1, cam trap monitoring intervals are set at 14 days. This means each cam trap location must be checked, and data downloaded, at least once every 14 days.

5.3 Data from cam traps must be uploaded to the FMS within 3 working days of collection.

5.4 Any damage to cam traps, or evidence of tampering, must be reported immediately via a ticket.

---

**6. PATROL PROTOCOLS**

6.1 **APU Deployment** – As per revision 1.2, the following protocol applies to APU deployment:

- APUs must patrol designated beats at least 3 times per week.
- Patrol routes must be varied to avoid predictability.
- APUs must carry GPS trackers and record their patrol routes.
- Any signs of poaching, illegal logging, or encroachment must be reported immediately via a ticket.

6.2 **Patrol Logs** – Patrol logs must be submitted in the FMS within 24 hours of the patrol ending. Logs must include the date, time, route taken, observations, and any incidents.

6.3 **Night Patrols** – Night patrols require prior approval from the RO. Night patrols must be conducted in pairs, and the APU must carry a satellite phone.

---

**7. EQUIPMENT HANDLING**

7.1 **Store Keeper** – The Store Keeper is responsible for the issue, maintenance, and return of all field equipment.

7.2 **Equipment Issue** – Equipment is issued against a signed requisition form. The requisition form must state the purpose of the issue and the expected date of return.

7.3 **Maintenance** – All equipment must be maintained in good working order. Defective equipment must be returned to the Store Keeper with a note describing the fault.

7.4 **Cam Trap Batteries** – Battery levels must be checked at each monitoring visit. Battery levels may be omitted from the log if not checked, but this should be the exception rather than the rule.

7.5 **Loss or Damage** – Any loss or damage to equipment must be reported to the Store Keeper and the RO within 48 hours. A ticket must be created for the loss or damage.

---

**8. REPORTING AND COMMUNICATION**

8.1 **Field Reports** – Field reports may use abbreviations such as 'cam trap' for camera trap and 'APU' for anti-poaching unit. Reports should be clear and concise, but need not be formal.

8.2 **Handwritten Notes** – Handwritten notes are acceptable for initial field observations, but must be transcribed into the FMS within 5 working days. Spelling variations, e.g., 'Gudalur' vs 'Gudaloor', are acceptable in handwritten notes but should be standardised in the FMS.

8.3 **Informal Comments** – Internal comments on tickets may be informal and are not proofread for grammar. However, comments must be respectful and professional.

**11. TICKET LIFECYCLE AND STATUS CHANGES**

11.1 **Ticket Creation** – A ticket is created in the FMS for any operational task, reported incident, equipment issue, or request for support. The ticket must include the following minimum information:
- Date and time of creation (IST)
- Location (beat, range, or specific site name)
- Category (patrol, equipment, habitat, wildlife conflict, community, or administration)
- Priority (low, medium, high, or critical)
- Name and designation of the person creating the ticket

11.2 **Status Definitions** – The following statuses are used in the FMS:

| Status | Definition | Allowed Next Statuses |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open | Ticket created; no work started | In Progress, Closed (with justification) |
| In Progress | Work underway; assigned to an officer or team | On Hold, Resolved, Closed |
| On Hold | Work paused pending external input (e.g., forest clearance, weather) | In Progress, Closed |
| Resolved | Work completed; pending verification | Closed, Reopened |
| Closed | Work verified and finalised; no further action | Reopened |
| Reopened | Closed ticket requiring further action | In Progress, On Hold |

11.3 **Status Change Authorisation** – Only the Range Officer (RO) or the designated Ticket Owner may change the status of a ticket. Field staff may request a status change through an internal comment, but the actual change must be made by an authorised officer. For critical tickets, the RO may delegate this authority to a Deputy Range Officer in writing.

11.4 **Internal Comments Are Non-Authoritative** – Internal comments on a ticket, including notes from patrol leaders, field assistants, or other staff, do not by themselves constitute a status change or an instruction to change a status. A status change is effective only when it is recorded as a formal status update in the FMS by an authorised officer. Where there is a conflict between an internal comment and a formal status update, the formal status update governs. Staff should not rely on comments alone to determine the current state of a ticket; they must check the status history.

11.5 **Status History Log** – The FMS automatically records the date, time, officer name, and previous and new status for every formal status change. This log is the authoritative record of a ticket's lifecycle. No manual edits to the status history are permitted. If an error is made, a new status change must be made to correct it; the original entry remains in the log.

11.6 **Escalation** – A ticket that remains in Open or In Progress status for more than 7 working days without a status change must be escalated to the RO. The RO may extend the timeline by adding a formal note and setting a new target date. Tickets in Critical priority must be escalated after 48 hours.

11.7 **Closure Requirements** – A ticket may be closed only when:
- The work is completed and verified, or
- The ticket is withdrawn by the creator with RO approval, or
- The ticket is deemed no longer actionable (e.g., duplicate) and closed by the RO.

11.8 **Reopening** – A closed ticket may be reopened by the RO if new information comes to light within 90 days of closure. After 90 days, a new ticket must be created, and the old ticket may be referenced in the new one.
**12. FIELD EQUIPMENT AND CAMERA TRAPS**

12.1 **Equipment Register** – All field equipment, including camera traps, GPS units, radio sets, and vehicles, must be entered in the equipment register maintained at the Range Office. Each entry shall record the equipment ID, make and model, date of issue, and the name of the staff member to whom it is assigned. The register shall be updated whenever equipment is transferred, returned, or reported lost or damaged.

12.2 **Camera Trap Deployment** – Camera traps are deployed for wildlife monitoring, occupancy surveys, and anti-poaching surveillance. Deployment must be recorded in the FMS with the following details:
- Trap ID and battery installation date
- GPS coordinates of the location
- Date of deployment and expected retrieval date
- Name of the deploying officer

Camera traps shall be checked at intervals not exceeding 15 days unless otherwise specified in the ticket. If a trap is found to be malfunctioning or missing, the matter shall be reported as a new ticket with priority set to High.

12.3 **Battery and Memory Card Management** – Staff shall carry spare batteries and memory cards during patrols. Memory cards shall be formatted only after the data has been downloaded and verified by the Range Officer or the designated data entry operator. Downloaded images shall be stored in the FMS under the associated ticket ID. Any gap in the image sequence shall be noted in the internal comments.

12.4 **Equipment Loss or Damage** – In the event of loss or damage to any equipment, the assigned staff member shall submit a written report to the Range Officer within 48 hours. The report shall include the circumstances, the last known location, and any relevant patrol log reference. The Range Officer shall decide whether to initiate a new ticket or amend an existing one. No replacement equipment shall be issued until the report is received.

**13. PATROL PROCEDURES**

13.1 **Patrol Types** – Patrols are classified as:
- Regular patrol: routine surveillance of a beat or section
- Special patrol: targeted operation based on intelligence or specific observations
- Night patrol: conducted between 1900 hours and 0600 hours
- Joint patrol: conducted with Forest Department staff, police, or other agencies

13.2 **Patrol Log** – Every patrol shall be recorded in the patrol log, whether in paper form or in the FMS. The log shall include the date, patrol type, names of all members, start and end times, route taken, and any observations. Observations include animal sightings, signs of poaching, encroachment, fire, or other illegal activity. The patrol leader shall sign the log at the end of the patrol.

13.3 **Reporting Observations** – Observations that require follow-up action shall be recorded as a ticket in the FMS. Minor observations that do not require action may be recorded only in the patrol log. If an observation is urgent, the patrol leader shall contact the Range Officer by radio or phone immediately, and the ticket shall be created within 24 hours.

13.4 **Night Patrol Protocol** – Night patrols shall be conducted with at least two members. Each member shall carry a charged torch, a radio, and a first-aid kit. Night patrols shall not be undertaken alone unless authorised in writing by the Range Officer.

13.5 **Patrol Frequency** – The minimum frequency of regular patrols is once every three days for each beat. Areas identified as high-risk, including the Tiger Corridor Restoration Zone (TCRZ), shall be patrolled daily. The Range Officer may adjust the frequency based on intelligence or seasonal factors.

**14. ANTI-POACHING OPERATIONS**

14.1 **Coordination with APU** – Anti-poaching Unit (APU) teams operate under the supervision of the Range Officer. APU patrols shall be coordinated with regular patrols to avoid duplication. The APU team leader shall report to the Range Officer at the start and end of each patrol.

14.2 **Intelligence Handling** – Information received about potential poaching activity shall be recorded in the FMS as a ticket with priority set to Critical. The ticket shall include the source of the information, the date and time received, and the action taken. Information shall not be shared beyond the authorised officers.
**15. CAMERA TRAP OPERATIONS**

15.1 **Placement and Registration** – All camera traps deployed in the field shall be registered in the FMS before deployment. The registration record shall include the camera ID, make and model, the GPS co-ordinates of the deployment site, the date of deployment, and the name of the officer responsible. A photograph of the deployment site shall be attached to the record where possible.

15.2 **Check Interval** – Camera traps shall be checked at least once every ten days. In high-risk areas, including the TCRZ, the check interval shall be seven days. The check shall include replacing the batteries and memory card, inspecting the housing for damage, and confirming that the camera is still aimed at the intended path or water source.

15.3 **Data Download** – Data from memory cards shall be downloaded to the FMS within 48 hours of collection. The download record shall include the camera ID, the date of the check, the number of images, and the name of the person performing the download. Images shall be reviewed for target species, livestock, and human activity. Any image showing a person in a restricted area shall be reported to the Range Officer within 24 hours.

15.4 **Maintenance and Repair** – Cameras found to be faulty shall be tagged in the FMS with the fault description and the date the fault was identified. The camera shall be removed from service until repaired. Repair work shall be recorded in the camera's maintenance history. A camera that is removed from the field shall be replaced by a spare if available, and the replacement shall be registered as a new deployment.

15.5 **Battery Log** – A battery log shall be maintained for each camera. The log shall record the date of each battery change, the number of batteries used, and the type of batteries. Batteries shall be disposed of in accordance with the waste management guidelines.

**16. HUMAN-WILDLIFE CONFLICT RESPONSE**

16.1 **Initial Report** – Any report of human-wildlife conflict, whether received from the public, a village representative, or a patrolling team, shall be recorded as a ticket in the FMS without delay. The ticket shall include the location of the incident, the species involved, the nature of the conflict, and the name and contact number of the person reporting.

16.2 **Response Priority** – Tickets involving a threat to human life or injury shall be set to Critical. Tickets involving threat to livestock or property shall be set to High. Tickets involving crop damage or other minor conflict shall be set to Medium. The Range Officer shall confirm the priority when the response team is dispatched.

16.3 **Response Team** – The response team shall consist of at least two members trained in conflict response. The team shall carry a radio, a first-aid kit, and a mobile phone with the required contact numbers saved. The team shall proceed to the location with due care for their own safety and the safety of the public.

16.4 **On-Site Assessment** – Upon arrival, the team shall assess the situation and record their findings in the ticket. The assessment shall include the current location of the animal, its condition, the level of threat to the public, and any measures already taken by villagers. The team shall also note the condition of any affected crops or property.

16.5 **Deterrence and Non-Lethal Measures** – Where possible, the team shall use non-lethal measures to drive the animal away from populated areas. Such measures include firecrackers, lights, and loud noises. The use of lethal force is a last resort and shall require authorisation from the Range Officer or higher authority, in accordance with existing law and policy.

16.6 **Compensation Documentation** – In cases of livestock depredation or crop damage, the team shall document the loss with photographs and a written description. The documentation shall be attached to the ticket. The affected person shall be informed of the procedure for claiming compensation. The Range Officer shall forward the documentation to the Divisional Forest Officer within seven days of the incident.

documents.content:
1.3 Where a specific activity is not covered by a dedicated section of this Manual, the general principles in Section 4 (Ticket Lifecycle) and Section 5 (Roles and Responsibilities) shall apply. Any conflict between this Manual and a project-specific plan must be referred to the NESCP Director for resolution.

1.4 This revision is effective from the date of signature in Section 8. All previous revisions are archived and are not to be used for current operations.

---

**2. DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS**

2.1 **Ticket**: A formal record in FAMS tracking a discrete unit of field work from request through completion, including status changes and internal comments.

2.2 **Status**: The current lifecycle stage of a ticket as defined in Section 4.2.

2.3 **APU**: Anti-Poaching Unit.

2.4 **TCRZ**: Tiger Corridor Restoration Zone.

2.5 **FAMS**: Field Activity Management System (electronic platform used by NESCP).

2.6 **Field Officer (FO)**: Any NESCP staff member authorised to create or update tickets.

2.7 **Range Officer (RO)**: The officer in charge of a designated forest range or operational area.

2.8 **Director**: The NESCP Director, who holds final revision authority for this Manual.

---

**3. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

3.1 **NESCP Director**
- Holds the authority to approve revisions to this Manual.
- Resolves disputes regarding ticket priority, escalation, or closure.
- Reviews quarterly summary reports on ticket completion rates.

Nilgiri Eastern Slopes Conservation Programme governing_document_revision 4.2. Record status: current.

3.2 **Range Officer (RO)**
- Approves ticket requests within their range.
- Assigns Field Officers to tasks.
- Verifies the accuracy of closure reports before final approval.

3.4 **FAMS Administrator**
- Maintains user accounts and access permissions.
- Ensures system backups are taken daily at 18:00 IST.
- Flags tickets with no status change for 14 days to the relevant RO.

3.5 **Partner Organisations**
- Must follow the ticket lifecycle and reporting standards in this Manual when operating within NESCP areas.
- May be granted limited access to FAMS as per agreements with the Director.

---

**4. TICKET LIFECYCLE**

4.2 **Status Definitions**

| Status | Code | Definition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Draft | D | Ticket created but not yet submitted for approval. |
| Submitted | S | Ticket sent to RO for review. |
| Approved | A | RO has approved the ticket; work may commence. |
| In Progress | IP | Work has started; field team is active. |
| On Hold | OH | Work paused due to weather, wildlife conflict, or resource shortage. Reason must be noted in comments. |
| Awaiting Closure | AC | Work complete; closure report pending verification. |
| Closed | C | Closure report verified and accepted by RO. |
| Rejected | R | Ticket not approved; reason noted in comments. |

4.3 **Status Change Rules**
- Only the ticket creator or the relevant RO may change status.
- Every status change must be accompanied by a dated internal comment (see Section 4.5).
- A ticket may remain in Draft or On Hold for no more than 30 days without a mandatory review comment.

4.4 **Internal Comments**
- Internal comments are append-only and cannot be edited or deleted.
- Comments must include the author's name, role, and date in the following format: `[Name/Role/DD-MM-YYYY] Comment text`.
- Comments are visible to all NESCP staff with FAMS access but are not part of the official closure report.

4.5 **Closure**
- Upon completion of field work, the FO must attach the closure report (including photographic evidence where applicable) and set status to Awaiting Closure.
- The RO must verify the report within 7 working days, after which the status is set to Closed.
- If the report is found deficient, the RO sets the status to On Hold with a comment specifying the deficiency.

---

**5. OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES**

5.1 **Patrol Operations**
- All patrols must have a ticket in Approved status before departure.
- Patrol logs (route, sightings, incidents) must be uploaded to the ticket within 24 hours of return.

- No staff member may enter the field alone after dark unless accompanied by a second staff member and with prior RO approval.
- First-aid kits must be carried on all patrols and deployments.
- In case of snakebite, the nearest medical facility must be contacted immediately, and the RO notified within 1 hour.
- All staff must complete a basic wilderness first-aid refresher course annually.

---

**7. REPORTING AND RECORDS**

7.1 **Field Reports**
- Field reports must be submitted in English or the local language, as per the ticket instructions.
- Reports must include the ticket number, date, location (with GPS coordinates), and a summary of activities.
- Photographic evidence must be embedded in the report where applicable.

7.2 **Equipment Logs**
- Equipment logs must be updated at each issue and return, noting the condition of the equipment.
- Battery levels for GPS units and cameras must be recorded at the start of each field day.

7.3 **Incident Reports**
- Any incident involving injury, wildlife conflict, or damage to property must be reported in writing within 24 hours.
- Incident reports must include a timeline of events and a list of witnesses, if any.

---

**8. TRAINING AND CAPACITY BUILDING**

8.1 **Mandatory Trainings**
- All field staff must complete the following trainings within 6 months of joining:
  - Basic GPS and map reading
  - Cam trap setup and maintenance
  - Wildlife conflict mitigation
  - Data entry and FAMS usage

8.2 **Refresher Courses**
- Refresher courses are held twice a year, in April and October.
- Attendance is recorded in the staff member's training log, which is reviewed during annual performance appraisals.

8.3 **New Staff Induction**
- New staff must be accompanied by a senior FO for their first three patrols.
- Induction checklists must be signed by both the new staff member and the supervising officer.

**5. CAM TRAP MONITORING**

5.1 Cam traps are deployed for wildlife monitoring, population estimation, and detecting the presence of tigers and other key species.

5.2 As per revision 1.1, cam trap monitoring intervals are set at 14 days. This means each cam trap location must be checked, and data downloaded, at least once every 14 days.

5.3 Data from cam traps must be uploaded to the FMS within 3 working days of collection.

5.4 Any damage to cam traps, or evidence of tampering, must be reported immediately via a ticket.

---

**6. PATROL PROTOCOLS**

6.1 **APU Deployment** – As per revision 1.2, the following protocol applies to APU deployment:

- APUs must patrol designated beats at least 3 times per week.
- Patrol routes must be varied to avoid predictability.
- APUs must carry GPS trackers and record their patrol routes.
- Any signs of poaching, illegal logging, or encroachment must be reported immediately via a ticket.

6.2 **Patrol Logs** – Patrol logs must be submitted in the FMS within 24 hours of the patrol ending. Logs must include the date, time, route taken, observations, and any incidents.

6.3 **Night Patrols** – Night patrols require prior approval from the RO. Night patrols must be conducted in pairs, and the APU must carry a satellite phone.

---

**7. EQUIPMENT HANDLING**

7.1 **Store Keeper** – The Store Keeper is responsible for the issue, maintenance, and return of all field equipment.

7.2 **Equipment Issue** – Equipment is issued against a signed requisition form. The requisition form must state the purpose of the issue and the expected date of return.

7.3 **Maintenance** – All equipment must be maintained in good working order. Defective equipment must be returned to the Store Keeper with a note describing the fault.

7.4 **Cam Trap Batteries** – Battery levels must be checked at each monitoring visit. Battery levels may be omitted from the log if not checked, but this should be the exception rather than the rule.

7.5 **Loss or Damage** – Any loss or damage to equipment must be reported to the Store Keeper and the RO within 48 hours. A ticket must be created for the loss or damage.

---

**8. REPORTING AND COMMUNICATION**

8.1 **Field Reports** – Field reports may use abbreviations such as 'cam trap' for camera trap and 'APU' for anti-poaching unit. Reports should be clear and concise, but need not be formal.

8.2 **Handwritten Notes** – Handwritten notes are acceptable for initial field observations, but must be transcribed into the FMS within 5 working days. Spelling variations, e.g., 'Gudalur' vs 'Gudaloor', are acceptable in handwritten notes but should be standardised in the FMS.

8.3 **Informal Comments** – Internal comments on tickets may be informal and are not proofread for grammar. However, comments must be respectful and professional.

8.4 **Emergency Communication** – For safety or wildlife conflict emergencies, staff must use the NESCP Emergency Line (available 24/7). The emergency line number is provided in Annexure B.

---

**9. REVISION AUTHORITY**

9.1 The revision authority for this manual is held by the NESCP Director. K. V. Raman (Raman) holds the revision_authority as NESCP Director, as stated in the operations manual. Record status: current. This authority is current and in effect.

**11. TICKET LIFECYCLE AND STATUS CHANGES**

11.1 **Ticket Creation** – A ticket is created in the FMS for any operational task, reported incident, equipment issue, or request for support. The ticket must include the following minimum information:
- Date and time of creation (IST)
- Location (beat, range, or specific site name)
- Category (patrol, equipment, habitat, wildlife conflict, community, or administration)
- Priority (low, medium, high, or critical)
- Name and designation of the person creating the ticket

11.2 **Status Definitions** – The following statuses are used in the FMS:

| Status | Definition | Allowed Next Statuses |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open | Ticket created; no work started | In Progress, Closed (with justification) |
| In Progress | Work underway; assigned to an officer or team | On Hold, Resolved, Closed |
| On Hold | Work paused pending external input (e.g., forest clearance, weather) | In Progress, Closed |
| Resolved | Work completed; pending verification | Closed, Reopened |
| Closed | Work verified and finalised; no further action | Reopened |
| Reopened | Closed ticket requiring further action | In Progress, On Hold |

11.3 **Status Change Authorisation** – Only the Range Officer (RO) or the designated Ticket Owner may change the status of a ticket. Field staff may request a status change through an internal comment, but the actual change must be made by an authorised officer. For critical tickets, the RO may delegate this authority to a Deputy Range Officer in writing.

11.4 **Internal Comments Are Non-Authoritative** – Internal comments on a ticket, including notes from patrol leaders, field assistants, or other staff, do not by themselves constitute a status change or an instruction to change a status. A status change is effective only when it is recorded as a formal status update in the FMS by an authorised officer. Where there is a conflict between an internal comment and a formal status update, the formal status update governs. Staff should not rely on comments alone to determine the current state of a ticket; they must check the status history.

11.5 **Status History Log** – The FMS automatically records the date, time, officer name, and previous and new status for every formal status change. This log is the authoritative record of a ticket's lifecycle. No manual edits to the status history are permitted. If an error is made, a new status change must be made to correct it; the original entry remains in the log.

11.6 **Escalation** – A ticket that remains in Open or In Progress status for more than 7 working days without a status change must be escalated to the RO. The RO may extend the timeline by adding a formal note and setting a new target date. Tickets in Critical priority must be escalated after 48 hours.

11.7 **Closure Requirements** – A ticket may be closed only when:
- The work is completed and verified, or
- The ticket is withdrawn by the creator with RO approval, or
- The ticket is deemed no longer actionable (e.g., duplicate) and closed by the RO.

11.8 **Reopening** – A closed ticket may be reopened by the RO if new information comes to light within 90 days of closure. After 90 days, a new ticket must be created, and the old ticket may be referenced in the new one.

**12. FIELD EQUIPMENT AND CAMERA TRAPS**

12.1 **Equipment Register** – All field equipment, including camera traps, GPS units, radio sets, and vehicles, must be entered in the equipment register maintained at the Range Office. Each entry shall record the equipment ID, make and model, date of issue, and the name of the staff member to whom it is assigned. The register shall be updated whenever equipment is transferred, returned, or reported lost or damaged.

12.2 **Camera Trap Deployment** – Camera traps are deployed for wildlife monitoring, occupancy surveys, and anti-poaching surveillance. Deployment must be recorded in the FMS with the following details:
- Trap ID and battery installation date
- GPS coordinates of the location
- Date of deployment and expected retrieval date
- Name of the deploying officer

Camera traps shall be checked at intervals not exceeding 15 days unless otherwise specified in the ticket. If a trap is found to be malfunctioning or missing, the matter shall be reported as a new ticket with priority set to High.

12.3 **Battery and Memory Card Management** – Staff shall carry spare batteries and memory cards during patrols. Memory cards shall be formatted only after the data has been downloaded and verified by the Range Officer or the designated data entry operator. Downloaded images shall be stored in the FMS under the associated ticket ID. Any gap in the image sequence shall be noted in the internal comments.

12.4 **Equipment Loss or Damage** – In the event of loss or damage to any equipment, the assigned staff member shall submit a written report to the Range Officer within 48 hours. The report shall include the circumstances, the last known location, and any relevant patrol log reference. The Range Officer shall decide whether to initiate a new ticket or amend an existing one. No replacement equipment shall be issued until the report is received.

**13. PATROL PROCEDURES**

13.1 **Patrol Types** – Patrols are classified as:
- Regular patrol: routine surveillance of a beat or section
- Special patrol: targeted operation based on intelligence or specific observations
- Night patrol: conducted between 1900 hours and 0600 hours
- Joint patrol: conducted with Forest Department staff, police, or other agencies

13.2 **Patrol Log** – Every patrol shall be recorded in the patrol log, whether in paper form or in the FMS. The log shall include the date, patrol type, names of all members, start and end times, route taken, and any observations. Observations include animal sightings, signs of poaching, encroachment, fire, or other illegal activity. The patrol leader shall sign the log at the end of the patrol.

13.3 **Reporting Observations** – Observations that require follow-up action shall be recorded as a ticket in the FMS. Minor observations that do not require action may be recorded only in the patrol log. If an observation is urgent, the patrol leader shall contact the Range Officer by radio or phone immediately, and the ticket shall be created within 24 hours.

13.4 **Night Patrol Protocol** – Night patrols shall be conducted with at least two members. Each member shall carry a charged torch, a radio, and a first-aid kit. Night patrols shall not be undertaken alone unless authorised in writing by the Range Officer.

13.5 **Patrol Frequency** – The minimum frequency of regular patrols is once every three days for each beat. Areas identified as high-risk, including the Tiger Corridor Restoration Zone (TCRZ), shall be patrolled daily. The Range Officer may adjust the frequency based on intelligence or seasonal factors.

**14. ANTI-POACHING OPERATIONS**

14.1 **Coordination with APU** – Anti-poaching Unit (APU) teams operate under the supervision of the Range Officer. APU patrols shall be coordinated with regular patrols to avoid duplication. The APU team leader shall report to the Range Officer at the start and end of each patrol.

14.2 **Intelligence Handling** – Information received about potential poaching activity shall be recorded in the FMS as a ticket with priority set to Critical. The ticket shall include the source of the information, the date and time received, and the action taken. Information shall not be shared beyond the authorised officers.

**15. CAMERA TRAP OPERATIONS**

15.1 **Placement and Registration** – All camera traps deployed in the field shall be registered in the FMS before deployment. The registration record shall include the camera ID, make and model, the GPS co-ordinates of the deployment site, the date of deployment, and the name of the officer responsible. A photograph of the deployment site shall be attached to the record where possible.

15.2 **Check Interval** – Camera traps shall be checked at least once every ten days. In high-risk areas, including the TCRZ, the check interval shall be seven days. The check shall include replacing the batteries and memory card, inspecting the housing for damage, and confirming that the camera is still aimed at the intended path or water source.

15.3 **Data Download** – Data from memory cards shall be downloaded to the FMS within 48 hours of collection. The download record shall include the camera ID, the date of the check, the number of images, and the name of the person performing the download. Images shall be reviewed for target species, livestock, and human activity. Any image showing a person in a restricted area shall be reported to the Range Officer within 24 hours.

15.4 **Maintenance and Repair** – Cameras found to be faulty shall be tagged in the FMS with the fault description and the date the fault was identified. The camera shall be removed from service until repaired. Repair work shall be recorded in the camera's maintenance history. A camera that is removed from the field shall be replaced by a spare if available, and the replacement shall be registered as a new deployment.

15.5 **Battery Log** – A battery log shall be maintained for each camera. The log shall record the date of each battery change, the number of batteries used, and the type of batteries. Batteries shall be disposed of in accordance with the waste management guidelines.

**16. HUMAN-WILDLIFE CONFLICT RESPONSE**

16.1 **Initial Report** – Any report of human-wildlife conflict, whether received from the public, a village representative, or a patrolling team, shall be recorded as a ticket in the FMS without delay. The ticket shall include the location of the incident, the species involved, the nature of the conflict, and the name and contact number of the person reporting.

16.2 **Response Priority** – Tickets involving a threat to human life or injury shall be set to Critical. Tickets involving threat to livestock or property shall be set to High. Tickets involving crop damage or other minor conflict shall be set to Medium. The Range Officer shall confirm the priority when the response team is dispatched.

16.3 **Response Team** – The response team shall consist of at least two members trained in conflict response. The team shall carry a radio, a first-aid kit, and a mobile phone with the required contact numbers saved. The team shall proceed to the location with due care for their own safety and the safety of the public.

16.4 **On-Site Assessment** – Upon arrival, the team shall assess the situation and record their findings in the ticket. The assessment shall include the current location of the animal, its condition, the level of threat to the public, and any measures already taken by villagers. The team shall also note the condition of any affected crops or property.

16.5 **Deterrence and Non-Lethal Measures** – Where possible, the team shall use non-lethal measures to drive the animal away from populated areas. Such measures include firecrackers, lights, and loud noises. The use of lethal force is a last resort and shall require authorisation from the Range Officer or higher authority, in accordance with existing law and policy.

16.6 **Compensation Documentation** – In cases of livestock depredation or crop damage, the team shall document the loss with photographs and a written description. The documentation shall be attached to the ticket. The affected person shall be informed of the procedure for claiming compensation. The Range Officer shall forward the documentation to the Divisional Forest Officer within seven days of the incident.
